title: Duplicate Emails
statement:
One table lists email addresses:

- `Person(id, email)`: `id` is unique; `email` is never `null` and is written in lowercase only. The same address may appear on several rows.

Find every email address that occurs on **two or more** rows. Return a single column named `Email`, listing each such address exactly once. Rows may come in any order.
reference:
SELECT email AS Email
FROM Person
GROUP BY email
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;
brute:
SELECT DISTINCT p.email AS Email
FROM Person AS p
WHERE EXISTS (
  SELECT 1
  FROM Person AS other
  WHERE other.email = p.email
    AND other.id <> p.id
)
notes:
## Intuition

An address is a duplicate when more than one row carries it. Grouping the rows by `email` collapses every address into one group whose size is the number of rows using it, so the duplicates are simply the groups with a count above 1. Grouping also guarantees each address is reported once, however many times it repeats.

## Approach

1. Read every row of `Person`.
2. `GROUP BY email` so each distinct address becomes one group.
3. `HAVING COUNT(*) > 1` keeps only the groups with at least two rows; `HAVING` is needed because the condition is about a group, not a single row.
4. Select the group key, renamed to `Email` as the output requires.

## Example 1, step by step

- Grouping by `email` gives two groups: `a@b.com` with ids 1 and 3 (count 2) and `c@d.com` with id 2 (count 1).
- `HAVING COUNT(*) > 1` keeps `a@b.com` and drops `c@d.com`.
- The result is one row: `Email = a@b.com`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n) with hash grouping over n rows, or O(n log n) if the database sorts to group.
- Space: O(d) for d distinct addresses.

## Pitfalls

- Filtering with `WHERE COUNT(*) > 1` is an error: aggregates are only available after grouping, in `HAVING`.
- A self-join on equal emails and different ids finds duplicates too, but without `DISTINCT` an address used three times is reported six times.
- The output column must be named `Email`; selecting plain `email` gives the wrong header on LeetCode.

## Clauses

| Name | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `GROUP BY email` | one group per distinct address |
| `COUNT(*)` | number of rows using that address |
| `HAVING COUNT(*) > 1` | keeps addresses that appear at least twice |
| `Email` | the output column, the group's address |

narration.1: Report the grouped address under the required column name Email.
narration.2: Every row of Person takes part.
narration.3: Group rows by address so each distinct email becomes one group.
narration.4: Keep only groups with more than one row: those addresses are duplicates.
